hypothesis: If unrelated demonstrations contributed to the 46.7% aggregate result, retrieving four cases by lexical and character overlap will exceed the 53.3% direct-prompt result while using less than 8,496 average context characters; otherwise this retrieval hypothesis is falsified.

If prior incorrect predictions contain reusable information, retrieving at most two similar failed attempts with their verified corrections will exceed the 53.3% aggregate direct-prompt result at lower context; otherwise this feedback mechanism is falsified.

If explicit context labels organize useful patterns, retaining up to three diverse verified examples per label will exceed the 53.3% aggregate direct-prompt result while staying below 8,496 average context characters; otherwise context routing is falsified.

Aggregate results favor no memory over unconditional retrieval, while pooled same-context overlap varies; retrieving one verified example only above a conservative overlap threshold should outperform always-on retrieval by reducing irrelevant context.
When a response-format contract repeats across prior inputs, repeating that contract at the end of the prompt should improve instruction adherence while preserving the full original problem.

When verified answers recur strongly within a declared context, a confidence-gated label-frequency prior should improve predictions; high uniqueness in the pooled traces should make it abstain on diffuse answer distributions.

The aggregate leader is no_memory at 53.3% with a 191-character context, while all systems that add retrieved memory score 40.0–46.7%. If excessive prompt additions contribute to answer drift, a short final format check without demonstrations will exceed 53.3%; a result at or below 53.3% falsifies this claim.

Pooled traces include near-miss outputs, so an independent second pass that checks a draft against the original constraints should raise aggregate accuracy above the 53.3% no_memory result; an equal or lower result falsifies this claim.

When a complete normalized input repeats with one consistent verified answer, returning that answer directly should correct the repeat while leaving unseen inputs on a direct-prompt fallback. The aggregate should improve only if such repeats occur; any fallback regression or incorrect cache hit falsifies the claim.

A task agnostic checklist pass before solving will improve exact instruction and response format adherence over direct prompting, which reached 53.3% aggregate accuracy; falsified if its aggregate validation accuracy is no higher than no_memory.
Reconciling two independent answers against the original task will resolve some single-pass reasoning errors; falsified if aggregate accuracy does not exceed the 53.3% no_memory baseline.

IDF-weighted retrieval of at most two same-context examples will provide more useful precedent than broad example inclusion while reducing prompt dilution; falsified if it fails to exceed the 43.3% sparse_retrieval_memory result.

On the pooled task distribution, routing only drafts flagged as concretely uncertain to a focused second solve will retain the direct and audited systems' accuracy while using fewer review calls than always auditing.

A single-pass prompt that separates decisive changes from preserved input information will outperform the plain direct prompt on aggregate accuracy by reducing unsupported edits to otherwise unchanged details.

Exact majority voting across three independent answer strings will improve aggregate accuracy over two-answer reconciliation when independent attempts converge, while explicit resolution is reserved for disagreement.

On the pooled validation set, explicitly identifying transformed regions and preserved scaffold before answer generation will outperform direct prompting on cases where the main scaffold is mostly unchanged.

On the pooled validation set, checking whether the proposed precursor set can plausibly regenerate the stated product will improve accuracy over a single draft, especially when the draft uses an incorrect leaving group or functional-group precursor.
